data.detail:
4/4 implement loops used; the conformance review still asks for fixes: [adversarial_reviewer] Stop git from running maintenance in the worker cache on its own, so that the repo-lock rule `_clear_stale_locks` depends on actually holds. Pass `--no-auto-maintenance` (or `--no-auto-gc`) to the cache `git fetch` in `_checkout`. Also set `gc.auto=0` and `maintenance.auto=false` in the cache config right after `git init --bare` (and for existing caches, under the repo lock), or pass them with `-c` on every cache git. That leaves the worker's own `gc()` as the only gc, and it runs under the repo lock. Then make `gc()` add a repo to `pruned` only when `git gc --prune=now` exits 0. Optionally: pass `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` for gate processes (a narrow change in `run_gate` that keeps local behaviour the same), and add a `stop.check()` after the clone/checkout so a signal there ends with the documented `signal` error. Add a test that runs a fetch on a cache with `gc.autoPackLimit=1` and asserts that no `gc.pid` or background gc is left after `_checkout` returns.

- [major] git fetch's detached auto-gc writes the cache outside the repo lock, so `_clear_stale_locks` can delete live git locks (src/nightwright/agentic/worker.py): `_checkout` runs `git -C cache fetch ... <bundle>` with no `--no-auto-maintenance`/`--no-auto-gc`, and the cache is created by a plain `git init --bare` with no `gc.auto=0`/`maintenance.auto=false`. By default git fetch runs `git maintenance run --auto` when it finishes. Once the cache passes `gc.autoPackLimit` (50 packs) or `gc.auto` (6700 loose objects), that becomes a `git gc --auto` that detaches into the background (gc/maintenance autoDetach is on by default). It keeps running after `_checkout` releases the repo lock. Each bundle fetch is unbundled through index-pack and adds a pack. The worker's own `gc()` only repacks when it removed refs, and that rarely happens within the 2-day keep window, because every job drops its own job refs before it calls gc. So on a busy worker, 50 jobs for one repo are enough to start a detached gc. This breaks the rule stated at worker.py:166-169 and in the spec ('every git that writes the cache runs under the repo lock, so a git lock file found while holding it is stale'). The next job, `have` or `gc` then deletes the detached gc's in-flight `packed-refs.lock` and `refs/**/*.lock` (pack-refs prune locks), so two writers act on the same refs. Other effects: the running gc's pack-refs fails; a concurrent `update-ref` (have refs, job-ref deletion) fails with 'unable to lock', which shows up as a `checkout` error or a silently orphaned job ref; and the explicit `git gc --prune=now` in `gc()` exits 'gc is already running' (check=False) while the repo is still listed in `pruned`, so the objects are not freed.
trigger: About 50 gate jobs for one repo_key within the keep window (each bundle fetch adds a pack). The next fetch starts a detached `git gc --auto` in the cache. A concurrent job, `have` or `gc` then takes the repo lock and runs `_clear_stale_locks` while that gc holds packed-refs.lock or refs/*.lock.

data.note: Fix the adversarial reviewer's finding: pass --no-auto-maintenance to the cache git fetch in _checkout, set gc.auto=0 and maintenance.auto=false on cache init (and existing caches under the repo lock), make gc() list a repo in pruned only on exit 0, add the gc.autoPackLimit=1 test. Optionally stdin=DEVNULL for gate processes and a stop.check() after clone/checkout. Keep the change narrow.
